# windows_dns_client (Resource)

Manages the DNS client settings of one network interface on a remote Windows host (`Set-DnsClientServerAddress` / `Set-DnsClient` via SSH and PowerShell). One resource owns one interface: creating a second resource for the same interface races the first (last writer wins for the managed families).

Managed versus unmanaged (`null` versus `[]`): every setting except `interface_alias` is `Optional` + `Computed` (partial management). `null` (omitted) leaves the host value untouched and undiffed; an explicitly empty list resets the family to automatic (DHCP). For example, omitting `ipv4_server_addresses` keeps whatever the host has (static or DHCP), while `ipv4_server_addresses = []` removes every static IPv4 server so the interface uses DHCP-provided servers only.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `null` (omitted) | Unmanaged: the host value is left untouched. |
| `[]` (empty) | Reset to automatic: static servers are removed, DHCP provides servers. Only meaningful on a configured (non-`null`) list. |
| `["a", "b"]` | Static: the listed servers replace the family in order. |

Static versus effective: `ipv4_server_addresses` / `ipv6_server_addresses` track the statically configured servers (registry `Tcpip`/`Tcpip6` `Interfaces\{guid}\NameServer`). `effective_ipv4` / `effective_ipv6` are read-only and DHCP-inclusive: they report the live servers from `Get-DnsClientServerAddress` (static plus DHCP-provided). When a family is automatic, the managed list is `[]` while the effective list shows the DHCP-provided servers.

Manage only secondary NICs with this resource: changing DNS on the management NIC can break name resolution for the host itself.

Import format: `<interface_alias>`. Import adopts the live state: both families become managed (automatic families import as `[]`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Static DNS servers on a secondary NIC (the management NIC keeps its own
# resolvers). Documentation ranges only (RFC 5737 / RFC 3849). Omitting a
# family leaves it unmanaged; an empty list resets it to automatic (DHCP).
resource "windows_dns_client" "secondary" {
  interface_alias       = "Ethernet 2"
  ipv4_server_addresses = ["192.0.2.53", "198.51.100.53"] # documentation range, RFC 5737
  ipv6_server_addresses = ["2001:db8::53"]                # documentation range, RFC 3849

  connection_specific_suffix       = "corp.example.com" # documentation range, RFC 2606
  register_this_connection_address = true
  use_suffix_when_registering      = true

  # Reset the managed families to automatic (DHCP) on destroy.
  reset_on_destroy = true

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly. Without this block each operation
  # defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a
  # timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "10m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "10m"
    delete = "10m"
  }
}

output "dns_effective_ipv4" {
  value       = windows_dns_client.secondary.effective_ipv4
  description = "Live IPv4 DNS servers (static plus DHCP-provided)."
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `interface_alias` (String) Network interface alias (e.g. `"Ethernet 2"`). Matched exactly and case-insensitively, never as a wildcard. Immutable after creation (ForceNew). The configured spelling is preserved in state; the id carries the trimmed form.

### Optional

- `connection_specific_suffix` (String) Connection-specific DNS suffix (e.g. `"corp.example.com"`). `null` leaves the suffix unmanaged. The suffix cannot be cleared in place: an empty string is rejected, and `null` leaves the host value untouched. To clear a managed suffix, destroy with `reset_on_destroy = true`. Must follow DNS name rules (labels of 1-63 letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit; total length at most 253).
- `ipv4_server_addresses` (List of String) Static IPv4 DNS servers in query order (first answer wins). `null` leaves the family unmanaged; `[]` resets it to automatic (DHCP); a list replaces the static servers. Loopback addresses are allowed; unspecified, multicast, limited broadcast (`255.255.255.255`) and zone-ID addresses are rejected, as are duplicates and IPv6 addresses.
- `ipv6_server_addresses` (List of String) Static IPv6 DNS servers in query order (first answer wins). `null` leaves the family unmanaged; `[]` resets it to automatic (DHCP); a list replaces the static servers. Addresses are stored canonically (lower-case, compressed) with the configured order preserved. Loopback addresses are allowed; unspecified, multicast and zone-ID addresses are rejected, as are duplicates and IPv4 addresses.
- `register_this_connection_address` (Boolean) Whether to register this connection's address in DNS (`Set-DnsClient -RegisterThisConnectionsAddress`). `null` leaves the flag unmanaged.
- `reset_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, destroy resets every managed family to automatic (DHCP) and clears the connection-specific suffix when it was managed. Defaults to `false`: destroy makes no remote change.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `use_suffix_when_registering` (Boolean) Whether to use the connection-specific suffix when registering in DNS (`Set-DnsClient -UseSuffixWhenRegistering`). `null` leaves the flag unmanaged.

### Read-Only

- `effective_ipv4` (List of String) Live IPv4 DNS servers, as observed on the host (static plus DHCP-provided).
- `effective_ipv6` (List of String) Live IPv6 DNS servers, as observed on the host (static plus DHCP-provided).
- `id` (String) Resource identifier: the canonical (trimmed) interface alias.
- `interface_guid` (String) Interface GUID (braces included), as observed on the host.
- `interface_index` (Number) Numeric interface index, as observed on the host.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import the DNS client settings of an existing interface by alias.
# Both families become managed (automatic families import as []).
terraform import windows_dns_client.secondary "Ethernet 2"
```
